ahimaaz_144.name: Ahimaaz
ahimaaz_144.who: A son of Zadok the priest who served as a swift messenger for David during Absalom's rebellion.
key: He and Jonathan, son of Abiathar, were stationed to carry news from Jerusalem to David (2 Samuel 15).
Hiding in a well at Bahurim, he escaped Absalom's men and warned David to cross the Jordan (2 Samuel 17).
After Absalom's defeat he outran the Cushite to bring David news of the victory (2 Samuel 18).
He is listed in the priestly line of Aaron as father of Azariah (1 Chronicles 6).

amoz_240.name: Amoz
amoz_240.who: The father of the prophet Isaiah, named whenever Scripture identifies Isaiah as the son of Amoz.
key: Isaiah's vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem is introduced as the vision of Isaiah son of Amoz (Isaiah 1).
Isaiah son of Amoz sent King Hezekiah God's answer concerning Sennacherib of Assyria (2 Kings 19).
Isaiah son of Amoz told the ill Hezekiah to set his house in order (2 Kings 20).

barak_401.name: Barak
barak_401.who: The son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali who led Israel's army against Sisera at Deborah's summons.
key: Deborah summoned him to lead ten thousand men, and he insisted she go with him (Judges 4).
He routed Sisera's army at Mount Tabor, though the honor of killing Sisera went to Jael (Judges 4).
He and Deborah sang a song celebrating the Lord's victory over the Canaanites (Judges 5).
He is named among those who through faith conquered kingdoms (Hebrews 11).

gad_1263.name: Gad
gad_1263.who: A prophet and seer in David's service who delivered the Lord's messages to the king.
key: He told David to leave the stronghold and go into the land of Judah (1 Samuel 22).
After David's census he offered the king a choice of three punishments from the Lord (2 Samuel 24).
He instructed David to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite (2 Samuel 24).
His records are cited as a source for the acts of King David (1 Chronicles 29).
Hezekiah arranged the Levite musicians according to commands of David, Gad, and Nathan (2 Chronicles 29).

hamor_1365.name: Hamor
hamor_1365.who: A Hivite prince of the land around Shechem and the father of Shechem, who violated Jacob's daughter Dinah.
key: Jacob bought a piece of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor for a hundred pieces of money (Genesis 33).
After his son seized Dinah, Hamor proposed intermarriage between his people and Jacob's family (Genesis 34).
Simeon and Levi killed Hamor and Shechem after the men of the city were circumcised (Genesis 34).
Joseph's bones were buried at Shechem on the land Jacob bought from Hamor's sons (Joshua 24).
Stephen recalled the tomb Abraham bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem (Acts 7).

hezron_1520.name: Hezron
hezron_1520.who: A grandson of Judah through Perez whose descendants included King David and, ultimately, Jesus.
key: He was among the family of Jacob who went down into Egypt (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Hezronites within the tribe of Judah (Numbers 26).
He appears in the line from Perez to David at the close of Ruth (Ruth 4).
At sixty he married the daughter of Machir, who bore him Segub (1 Chronicles 2).
He is listed among the ancestors of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1).

hushai_1577.name: Hushai
hushai_1577.who: An Archite and trusted friend of King David who defeated Ahithophel's counsel during Absalom's revolt.
key: When David fled Jerusalem, he sent Hushai back to frustrate Ahithophel's advice (2 Samuel 15).
Hushai greeted Absalom and offered his service, gaining access to the usurper's council (2 Samuel 16).
His advice prevailed over Ahithophel's, and he secretly sent word for David to escape (2 Samuel 17).
He is recorded as the king's friend among David's officials (1 Chronicles 27).

jeduthun_1224.name: Jeduthun
jeduthun_1224.who: A Levite musician appointed by David to lead praise and thanksgiving to the Lord with lyres and other instruments.
key: He was appointed with Heman to give thanks to the Lord before the tabernacle at Gibeon (1 Chronicles 16).
David set apart his sons to prophesy with lyres in thanksgiving and praise (1 Chronicles 25).
His musicians stood with Asaph and Heman when the ark was brought into Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 5).
He is called the king's seer when Josiah kept the Passover (2 Chronicles 35).
The heading of Psalm 77 directs it to the choirmaster according to Jeduthun (Psalm 77).

kish_1784.name: Kish
kish_1784.who: A wealthy Benjaminite, son of Abiel, best known as the father of Saul, Israel's first king.
key: He sent his son Saul to search for lost donkeys, a journey that led Saul to Samuel (1 Samuel 9).
When Saul prophesied among the prophets, people asked what had happened to the son of Kish (1 Samuel 10).
The bones of Saul and Jonathan were buried in the tomb of Kish in Benjamin (2 Samuel 21).
Paul recalled that God gave Israel Saul the son of Kish as king (Acts 13).

omri_2243.name: Omri
omri_2243.who: An army commander who became king of Israel, founded Samaria as its capital, and was father of Ahab.
key: The army made him king after Zimri murdered King Elah, and he besieged Tirzah (1 Kings 16).
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built the city there (1 Kings 16).
He did more evil in the Lord's sight than all who were before him (1 Kings 16).
Athaliah, who later seized Judah's throne, was his granddaughter (2 Kings 8).
Micah condemned Israel for keeping the statutes of Omri (Micah 6).

remaliah_2420.name: Remaliah
remaliah_2420.who: The father of Pekah, who seized the throne of Israel; Isaiah refers to Pekah simply as Remaliah's son.
key: Pekah son of Remaliah conspired against King Pekahiah and reigned over Israel in Samaria (2 Kings 15).
Pekah son of Remaliah killed a great number of Judah's soldiers in one day (2 Chronicles 28).
Isaiah assured Ahaz that the son of Remaliah would not succeed against Judah (Isaiah 7).

ruth_2450.name: Ruth
ruth_2450.who: A Moabite widow who stayed loyal to Naomi, married Boaz, and became the great-grandmother of King David.
key: After her husband died, she refused to leave Naomi and committed herself to Naomi's God (Ruth 1).
She gleaned barley in the field of Boaz, who showed her protective kindness (Ruth 2).
At Naomi's direction she asked Boaz at the threshing floor to act as redeemer (Ruth 3).
Boaz redeemed Naomi's land and married Ruth, and she bore Obed, David's grandfather (Ruth 4).
She is named in the genealogy of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1).

tamar_2822.name: Tamar
tamar_2822.who: A daughter of King David and full sister of Absalom, who was violated by her half brother Amnon.
key: Amnon tricked her into his room, forced her, and then sent her away in disgrace (2 Samuel 13).
She lived desolate in Absalom's house, and Absalom later had Amnon killed (2 Samuel 13).
She is listed as the sister of David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3).

ziba_3060.name: Ziba
ziba_3060.who: A servant of Saul's household whom David appointed to farm the land restored to Mephibosheth.
key: He told David about Jonathan's son Mephibosheth and was put in charge of his land (2 Samuel 9).
He met the fleeing David with supplies and accused Mephibosheth of disloyalty, receiving his property (2 Samuel 16).
He hurried to the Jordan to meet the returning king with his sons and servants (2 Samuel 19).
After Mephibosheth explained himself, David ordered Ziba and Mephibosheth to divide the land (2 Samuel 19).

abihu_33.name: Abihu
abihu_33.who: The second son of Aaron, ordained as a priest, who died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord.
key: He went up Mount Sinai with Moses and the elders and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24).
He was set apart with his brothers to serve the Lord as a priest (Exodus 28).
He and Nadab offered unauthorized fire, and fire from the Lord consumed them (Leviticus 10).
He died without children, so the priesthood passed through Eleazar and Ithamar (Numbers 3).

agrippa_111.name: Agrippa
agrippa_111.who: King Agrippa II, a ruler of the Herod family who heard the apostle Paul's defense at Caesarea.
key: He and Bernice visited Festus, who told them about Paul's case (Acts 25).
Festus brought Paul before Agrippa to help frame charges for the emperor (Acts 25).
Paul told Agrippa of his conversion and urged him to believe the prophets (Acts 26).
Agrippa judged that Paul could have been freed had he not appealed to Caesar (Acts 26).

andrew_264.name: Andrew
andrew_264.who: A fisherman from Bethsaida, brother of Simon Peter, and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
key: A disciple of John the Baptist, he followed Jesus and brought his brother Simon to him (John 1).
Jesus called him and Peter from their nets to become fishers of men (Matthew 4).
He brought Jesus a boy with five barley loaves and two fish (John 6).
He and Philip told Jesus that some Greeks wished to see him (John 12).
He was with the apostles in the upper room after Jesus' ascension (Acts 1).

eber_1030.name: Eber
eber_1030.who: A descendant of Shem through Shelah, father of Peleg and Joktan, and an ancestor of Abraham.
key: He is named in the table of nations, where Shem is called the father of all Eber's children (Genesis 10).
He fathered Peleg at thirty-four and lived many years afterward (Genesis 11).
Balaam's final oracle foretold that ships would afflict Eber (Numbers 24).
He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).

gehazi_1293.name: Gehazi
gehazi_1293.who: The servant of the prophet Elisha, later struck with leprosy for greedily taking gifts from Naaman.
key: He told Elisha that the Shunammite woman had no son, and later laid Elisha's staff on her dead boy (2 Kings 4).
He secretly ran after Naaman, took silver and clothing, and lied to Elisha (2 Kings 5).
Elisha declared that Naaman's leprosy would cling to Gehazi, and he left leprous (2 Kings 5).
He was telling the king of Elisha's deeds when the Shunammite woman arrived to appeal (2 Kings 8).

hagar_1348.name: Hagar
hagar_1348.who: An Egyptian servant of Sarah who bore Abraham's son Ishmael and was twice met by the angel of the Lord.
key: Sarai gave her to Abram as a wife; when mistreated she fled, and the angel of the Lord met her (Genesis 16).
She called the Lord the God who sees her, and bore Ishmael (Genesis 16).
Sent away with Ishmael, she wept in the wilderness until God opened her eyes to a well (Genesis 21).
Paul used Hagar and Sarah as an allegory of two covenants (Galatians 4).

heman_1490.name: Heman
heman_1490.who: A Levite singer of the Kohathite line, grandson of Samuel, appointed by David as a leading temple musician.
key: He is listed as a singer descended from Kohath, son of Joel and grandson of Samuel (1 Chronicles 6).
The Levites appointed him with Asaph and Ethan to sound bronze cymbals before the ark (1 Chronicles 15).
Called the king's seer, he had fourteen sons and three daughters who served in temple music (1 Chronicles 25).
He and his musicians praised the Lord as the glory cloud filled Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 5).

heth_1510.name: Heth
heth_1510.who: A son of Canaan and ancestor of the Hittites, from whom Abraham bought a burial place.
key: He is listed as a son of Canaan in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah from the Hittites, the descendants of Heth (Genesis 23).
Esau's Hittite wives made Rebekah weary of her life (Genesis 27).
Jacob asked to be buried in the cave purchased from the Hittites (Genesis 49).

hur_1571.name: Hur
hur_1571.who: A man of Judah, son of Caleb and Ephrathah, and grandfather of Bezalel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
key: The Lord chose Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, to make the tabernacle and its furnishings (Exodus 31).
Moses announced to Israel that the Lord had called Hur's grandson Bezalel by name (Exodus 35).
He was born to Caleb and Ephrathah and became the father of Uri (1 Chronicles 2).
He is listed as the firstborn of Ephrathah and the father of Bethlehem (1 Chronicles 4).
Solomon worshiped at the bronze altar that Hur's grandson Bezalel had made (2 Chronicles 1).

josedech_815.name: Jehozadak
josedech_815.who: A priest, son of Seraiah, taken into exile by Nebuchadnezzar and father of Joshua the high priest.
key: He went into exile when the Lord sent Judah and Jerusalem away by Nebuchadnezzar (1 Chronicles 6).
His son Jeshua led the priests in rebuilding the altar after the return (Ezra 3).
His son Joshua the high priest was addressed with Zerubbabel through Haggai's prophecy (Haggai 1).
Zechariah set a crown on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak (Zechariah 6).

martha_1937.name: Martha
martha_1937.who: A woman of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, who welcomed Jesus into her home.
key: She welcomed Jesus, became anxious with serving, and was told Mary had chosen the good portion (Luke 10).
When Lazarus died, she met Jesus and confessed him as the Christ, the Son of God (John 11).
She served at a dinner for Jesus in Bethany six days before the Passover (John 12).

miriam_2087.name: Miriam
miriam_2087.who: A prophetess, sister of Moses and Aaron, who led Israel's women in praise after the Red Sea crossing.
key: She took a tambourine and led the women in singing to the Lord after the Red Sea crossing (Exodus 15).
She and Aaron spoke against Moses, and she was struck with leprosy for seven days (Numbers 12).
She died and was buried at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin (Numbers 20).
Moses told Israel to remember what the Lord did to Miriam (Deuteronomy 24).
Micah recalled that God sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam before his people (Micah 6).

nadab_2128.name: Nadab
nadab_2128.who: The firstborn son of Aaron, ordained as a priest, who died for offering unauthorized fire before the Lord.
key: He went up Mount Sinai with Moses and the elders and saw the God of Israel (Exodus 24).
He was set apart with his brothers to serve the Lord as a priest (Exodus 28).
He and Abihu offered unauthorized fire, and fire from the Lord consumed them (Leviticus 10).
He died without children, so the priesthood passed through Eleazar and Ithamar (Numbers 3).

pharaoh_2336.name: Pharaoh Hophra
pharaoh_2336.who: The king of Egypt in Zedekiah's day, named Hophra by Jeremiah, whose downfall Jeremiah and Ezekiel announced.
key: Jeremiah announced that Pharaoh Hophra would be given into his enemies' hands (Jeremiah 44).
Ezekiel condemned Zedekiah for breaking his oath and seeking help from Egypt (Ezekiel 17).
Ezekiel likened Pharaoh to a great monster claiming the Nile as his own (Ezekiel 29).
The Lord declared that he had broken Pharaoh's arm and would strengthen Babylon's king (Ezekiel 30).
Ezekiel raised a lament over Pharaoh, foretelling his fall among the slain (Ezekiel 32).

portius_2367.name: Porcius Festus
portius_2367.who: The Roman governor of Judea who succeeded Felix and heard Paul's case, sending him to Caesar.
key: He succeeded Felix as governor while Paul remained in custody (Acts 24).
He heard Paul at Caesarea, and Paul appealed to Caesar rather than go to Jerusalem (Acts 25).
He laid Paul's case before King Agrippa, admitting he found no capital crime (Acts 25).
During Paul's defense, Festus loudly said Paul's great learning was driving him mad (Acts 26).

thomas_2851.name: Thomas
thomas_2851.who: One of the twelve apostles, called the Twin, remembered for doubting and then confessing the risen Jesus.
key: He was named among the twelve apostles Jesus sent out (Matthew 10).
When Jesus went to Lazarus, Thomas urged the disciples to go and die with him (John 11).
He asked Jesus how they could know the way, and Jesus answered that he is the way (John 14).
He refused to believe without seeing, then confessed Jesus as his Lord and God (John 20).
He was with the disciples when the risen Jesus appeared at the Sea of Tiberias (John 21).

titus_2869.name: Titus
titus_2869.who: A Greek believer and trusted coworker of Paul, entrusted with ministry in Corinth and Crete.
key: He went with Paul to Jerusalem and was not compelled to be circumcised (Galatians 2).
Paul had no rest in Troas because he did not find Titus there (2 Corinthians 2).
Titus brought Paul comforting news of the Corinthians' repentance (2 Corinthians 7).
Paul sent him to Corinth to complete the collection for the saints (2 Corinthians 8).
Paul left him in Crete to appoint elders in every town (Titus 1).

tobiah_2872.name: Tobiah
tobiah_2872.who: An Ammonite official who repeatedly opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.
key: He and Sanballat were displeased that someone had come to seek Israel's welfare (Nehemiah 2).
He mocked the wall, saying even a fox would break it down (Nehemiah 4).
He sent letters to frighten Nehemiah and had many allies among Judah's nobles (Nehemiah 6).
Nehemiah threw his goods out of the temple chamber Eliashib had prepared for him (Nehemiah 13).

zerah_2984.name: Zerah
zerah_2984.who: A son of Judah and Tamar, twin brother of Perez, and ancestor of the Zerahite clan.
key: At his birth a scarlet thread was tied on his hand, but his twin Perez came out first (Genesis 38).
He went down to Egypt with the family of Jacob (Genesis 46).
His descendants formed the clan of the Zerahites in Judah (Numbers 26).
Achan, who took devoted things at Jericho, was a descendant of Zerah (Joshua 7).
He appears with Perez and Tamar in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

ahijah_135.name: Ahijah
ahijah_135.who: A prophet from Shiloh who foretold Jeroboam's rule over ten tribes and later the downfall of his house.
key: He tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave ten to Jeroboam (1 Kings 11).
The division of the kingdom fulfilled the word the Lord spoke through Ahijah (1 Kings 12).
Though blind, he recognized Jeroboam's disguised wife and foretold judgment on Jeroboam's house (1 Kings 14).
Baasha destroyed Jeroboam's whole house, according to the word spoken by Ahijah (1 Kings 15).
His prophecy is cited as a record of Solomon's acts (2 Chronicles 9).

ahimelech_126.name: Ahimelech
ahimelech_126.who: The priest at Nob, son of Ahitub, who helped David and was killed by Saul's order.
key: He gave the fleeing David holy bread and the sword of Goliath (1 Samuel 21).
Saul accused him of conspiracy, and Doeg the Edomite killed him and the priests of Nob (1 Samuel 22).
His son Abiathar escaped the massacre and fled to David (1 Samuel 22).
Abiathar brought an ephod with him when he came to David at Keilah (1 Samuel 23).

amasa_207.name: Amasa
amasa_207.who: A nephew of David, son of Abigail, who commanded Absalom's army and later David's, until Joab killed him.
key: Absalom appointed him commander of the army in place of Joab (2 Samuel 17).
After the revolt David promised to make him commander instead of Joab (2 Samuel 19).
Joab killed him at Gibeon while pretending to greet him with a kiss (2 Samuel 20).
David charged Solomon to deal with Joab for murdering Abner and Amasa (1 Kings 2).

amminadab_228.name: Amminadab
amminadab_228.who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, father of Nahshon, and an ancestor of King David and of Jesus.
key: His daughter Elisheba married Aaron (Exodus 6).
His son Nahshon was appointed chief of the tribe of Judah (Numbers 1).
He appears in the line from Perez to David (Ruth 4).
He is listed among the ancestors of Jesus Christ (Matthew 1).

amram_242.name: Amram
amram_242.who: A Levite of the clan of Kohath, husband of Jochebed, and father of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
key: He married his father's sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses; he lived 137 years (Exodus 6).
His descendants formed the clan of the Amramites among the Kohathites (Numbers 3).
Jochebed bore to Amram Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam (Numbers 26).
His son Aaron was set apart to make offerings before the Lord (1 Chronicles 23).

bathsheba_416.name: Bathsheba
bathsheba_416.who: The wife of Uriah whom David took in adultery; she later married David and became Solomon's mother.
key: David saw her bathing, slept with her, and arranged Uriah's death in battle (2 Samuel 11).
Their first child died, and she later bore Solomon, whom the Lord loved (2 Samuel 12).
With Nathan the prophet, she reminded David of his promise that Solomon would reign (1 Kings 1).
She brought Adonijah's request for Abishag to Solomon, who refused it (1 Kings 2).
She is listed as the mother of four of David's sons born in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3).

gilead_1317.name: Gilead
gilead_1317.who: A son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, ancestor of the Gileadite clans of that tribe.
key: His sons headed the clans of Manasseh counted in the second census (Numbers 26).
The daughters of Zelophehad, descendants of Gilead, asked for their father's inheritance (Numbers 27).
Heads of Gilead's clans raised concerns about inheritance passing to other tribes (Numbers 36).
His descendants received their allotment within the tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 17).

haggai_1349.name: Haggai
haggai_1349.who: A prophet to the returned exiles who urged them to finish rebuilding the temple in Jerusalem.
key: He and Zechariah prophesied to the Jews, and the rebuilding of the temple resumed (Ezra 5).
He rebuked the people for living in paneled houses while the Lord's house lay in ruins (Haggai 1).
He promised that the latter glory of the temple would be greater than the former (Haggai 2).
The temple was completed as the elders prospered through his prophesying (Ezra 6).

hannah_1400.name: Hannah
hannah_1400.who: A wife of Elkanah whose prayer for a son was answered with the birth of the prophet Samuel.
key: Childless and provoked by Peninnah, she prayed at Shiloh and vowed to give her son to the Lord (1 Samuel 1).
Eli thought she was drunk, then blessed her, and she later bore Samuel (1 Samuel 1).
She brought young Samuel to Eli and dedicated him to the Lord (1 Samuel 1).
Her prayer exalted the Lord who humbles the proud and lifts up the poor (1 Samuel 2).
The Lord gave her three more sons and two daughters (1 Samuel 2).

ish-bosheth_622.name: Ish-bosheth
ish-bosheth_622.who: A son of Saul whom Abner made king over Israel for two years after Saul's death.
key: Abner made him king over Israel while Judah followed David (2 Samuel 2).
He accused Abner over Saul's concubine, and Abner turned to support David (2 Samuel 3).
At David's demand he took Michal from her husband and returned her to David (2 Samuel 3).
Rechab and Baanah murdered him in his bed, and David executed them (2 Samuel 4).

japheth_726.name: Japheth
japheth_726.who: One of Noah's three sons, who survived the flood in the ark and became ancestor of many nations.
key: He is named as a son of Noah, along with Shem and Ham (Genesis 5).
He entered the ark with his wife, his parents, and his brothers (Genesis 7).
He and Shem covered their father's nakedness, and Noah blessed him (Genesis 9).
His descendants spread out as the peoples of the coastlands (Genesis 10).

lazarus_1812.name: Lazarus
lazarus_1812.who: A man of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, whom Jesus loved and raised from the dead.
key: He fell ill and died, and Jesus came to Bethany after he had been in the tomb four days (John 11).
Jesus wept, then called him out of the tomb alive (John 11).
He reclined at table with Jesus at a dinner in Bethany (John 12).
The chief priests planned to kill him because many believed in Jesus on his account (John 12).

mary_1939.name: Mary of Bethany
mary_1939.who: A woman of Bethany, sister of Martha and Lazarus, who sat at Jesus' feet and later anointed him.
key: She sat at the Lord's feet listening, and Jesus said she had chosen the good portion (Luke 10).
After Lazarus died, she fell at Jesus' feet weeping, and Jesus was deeply moved (John 11).
She anointed Jesus' feet with costly nard and wiped them with her hair (John 12).

melchisedec_1991.name: Melchizedek
melchisedec_1991.who: The king of Salem and priest of God Most High who blessed Abram, a type of Christ's priesthood.
key: He brought out bread and wine, blessed Abram, and received a tenth of everything (Genesis 14).
The psalmist declared the Lord's king a priest forever after his order (Psalm 110).
Hebrews teaches that Christ was designated high priest after the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 5).
Hebrews explains that he was greater than Levi's priests, since Abraham gave him a tenth (Hebrews 7).

naaman_2122.name: Naaman
naaman_2122.who: A commander of the army of Syria who was healed of leprosy after obeying the prophet Elisha.
key: An Israelite servant girl told his wife that the prophet in Samaria could heal him (2 Kings 5).
Angered at first, he washed seven times in the Jordan and was made clean (2 Kings 5).
He declared there is no God in all the earth but in Israel (2 Kings 5).
Jesus cited him as the only leper cleansed in Elisha's time (Luke 4).

nahshon_2144.name: Nahshon
nahshon_2144.who: The son of Amminadab and leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness, an ancestor of David and Jesus.
key: His sister Elisheba married Aaron (Exodus 6).
He was appointed chief of the tribe of Judah to help Moses take the census (Numbers 1).
On the first day of the altar's dedication, he presented Judah's offering (Numbers 7).
He led Judah's company at the front when Israel set out from Sinai (Numbers 10).
He appears in the line of David and in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

pekah_2299.name: Pekah
pekah_2299.who: A captain who killed King Pekahiah and reigned over Israel in Samaria, allying with Syria against Judah.
key: He conspired against Pekahiah, killed him, and reigned in his place for twenty years (2 Kings 15).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured many of his cities, and Hoshea assassinated him (2 Kings 15).
He and Rezin of Syria besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem but could not conquer him (2 Kings 16).
He killed 120,000 men of Judah in one day because they had forsaken the Lord (2 Chronicles 28).
Isaiah declared that the plot of Rezin and Pekah against Judah would not stand (Isaiah 7).

shealtiel_2456.name: Shealtiel
shealtiel_2456.who: A son of Jehoiachin, the captive king of Judah, and father of Zerubbabel, who led the return from exile.
key: He is listed among the sons of Jeconiah the captive (1 Chronicles 3).
His son Zerubbabel helped rebuild the altar of the God of Israel (Ezra 3).
Haggai's word came to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah (Haggai 1).
He appears after the deportation to Babylon in the genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1).

uzziel_2929.name: Uzziel
uzziel_2929.who: A Levite, son of Kohath and uncle of Moses and Aaron, whose descendants served at the tabernacle.
key: He is listed as a son of Kohath, and his sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri (Exodus 6).
Moses called his sons to carry away the bodies of Nadab and Abihu (Leviticus 10).
His son Elizaphan was made chief of the Kohathite clans (Numbers 3).
His descendants helped bring the ark to Jerusalem under David (1 Chronicles 15).

zebedee_2998.name: Zebedee
zebedee_2998.who: A Galilean fisherman and the father of the apostles James and John.
key: His sons James and John left him in the boat to follow Jesus (Matthew 4).
He had hired servants who worked with him in the fishing boat (Mark 1).
The mother of Zebedee's sons asked Jesus for places of honor for them (Matthew 20).
The mother of Zebedee's sons watched from a distance at the crucifixion (Matthew 27).
The sons of Zebedee were fishing when the risen Jesus appeared at the sea (John 21).

apollos_276.name: Apollos
apollos_276.who: A Jewish believer from Alexandria, eloquent in the Scriptures, who ministered in Ephesus and Corinth.
key: Priscilla and Aquila explained the way of God more accurately to him in Ephesus (Acts 18).
In Achaia he powerfully refuted the Jews, showing from Scripture that Jesus was the Christ (Acts 18).
Paul rebuked the Corinthians for dividing over Paul, Apollos, and Cephas (1 Corinthians 1).
Paul wrote that he planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth (1 Corinthians 3).
Paul asked Titus to speed Apollos on his way (Titus 3).

arphaxad_312.name: Arpachshad
arphaxad_312.who: A son of Shem born two years after the flood, and an ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus.
key: He is listed among the sons of Shem in the table of nations (Genesis 10).
Born two years after the flood, he fathered Shelah at thirty-five (Genesis 11).
He appears in the genealogy from Adam to Abraham (1 Chronicles 1).
He is named in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).

artaxerxes_314.name: Artaxerxes
artaxerxes_314.who: A king of Persia who authorized Ezra's mission and sent his cupbearer Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem.
key: The temple was finished according to decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes (Ezra 6).
He issued a letter granting Ezra authority, funds, and supplies for the temple (Ezra 7).
Seeing Nehemiah's sadness, he sent him to rebuild Jerusalem with letters and an escort (Nehemiah 2).
Nehemiah served as governor of Judah from Artaxerxes' twentieth to thirty-second year (Nehemiah 5).
Nehemiah returned to the king, then came back to Jerusalem to correct abuses (Nehemiah 13).

barabbas_399.name: Barabbas
barabbas_399.who: A notorious prisoner whom Pilate released at the crowd's demand instead of Jesus.
key: Pilate offered to release Jesus or Barabbas, and the crowd chose Barabbas (Matthew 27).
He had been imprisoned with rebels who had committed murder in an insurrection (Mark 15).
Pilate released the man jailed for insurrection and murder and delivered Jesus over (Luke 23).
John identifies Barabbas as a robber (John 18).

bilhah_502.name: Bilhah
bilhah_502.who: Rachel's servant, given to Jacob as a wife, who bore him Dan and Naphtali.
key: Laban gave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her servant (Genesis 29).
Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob, and she bore Dan and Naphtali (Genesis 30).
Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard of it (Genesis 35).
Young Joseph worked with the sons of Bilhah and brought a bad report about them (Genesis 37).

cornelius_956.name: Cornelius
cornelius_956.who: A God-fearing Roman centurion at Caesarea whose household received the Holy Spirit through Peter's preaching.
key: A devout centurion who prayed and gave alms, he saw an angel in a vision (Acts 10).
At the angel's word he sent men to Joppa to bring Simon Peter (Acts 10).
He gathered relatives and friends, and Peter preached that God shows no partiality (Acts 10).
The Holy Spirit fell on all who heard, and they were baptized in Jesus' name (Acts 10).

elkanah_1168.name: Elkanah
elkanah_1168.who: An Ephraimite of Ramathaim-zophim, husband of Hannah and Peninnah, and father of the prophet Samuel.
key: He went up yearly to worship at Shiloh and gave Hannah a double portion (1 Samuel 1).
He comforted Hannah in her grief and agreed to her vow concerning Samuel (1 Samuel 1).
Eli blessed Elkanah and Hannah, praying the Lord would give them more children (1 Samuel 2).
He appears in the Levitical genealogy of the singers as Samuel's father (1 Chronicles 6).

enoch_1192.name: Enoch
enoch_1192.who: A descendant of Seth, son of Jared, who walked with God and was taken by God without dying.
key: He fathered Methuselah, walked with God, and was no more, for God took him (Genesis 5).
He is listed in the line from Adam to Noah (1 Chronicles 1).
He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luke 3).
By faith he was taken up so that he should not see death (Hebrews 11).
Jude cites his prophecy of the Lord coming with his holy ones in judgment (Jude 1).

ephron_1208.name: Ephron
ephron_1208.who: A Hittite, son of Zohar, who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah as a family tomb.
key: He sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah for four hundred shekels of silver (Genesis 23).
Isaac and Ishmael buried Abraham in the cave in Ephron's former field (Genesis 25).
Jacob charged his sons to bury him in the cave in the field of Ephron (Genesis 49).
Jacob's sons buried him in the cave Abraham had bought from Ephron (Genesis 50).
